question.text: Tangent is drawn at any point $P$ of a curve which passes through $(1,1)$ cutting $X$-axis and $Y$-axis at $A$ and $B$, respectively. If $A P: B P=3: 1$, then

options.text: differential equation of the curve is $3 x \frac{d y}{d x}+y=0$
differential equation of the curve is $3 x \frac{d y}{d x}-y=0$

solution.text: Since, $\quad A P: B P=3: 1$ where, equation of tangent is $y-y_1=f^{\prime}(x)\left(x-x_1\right)$ $$ \begin{aligned} \therefore & A\left(x_1-\frac{y_1}{f^{\prime}\left(x_1\right)}, 0\right) \text { and } B\left(0, y_1-x_1 f^{\prime}(x)\right) \\ & A P: B P=3: 1 \Rightarrow \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{y}{-3 x} \\ \therefore \quad & 3 x \frac{d y}{d x}+y=0 \quad \text { or } \quad \frac{d y}{y}=-\frac{1}{3 x} d x, \end{aligned} $$ On integrating both sides, we get $$ \begin{array}{lrlr} \Rightarrow & x y^3 & =1 \\ & \therefore \text { At } & x & =\frac{1}{8} \quad \text { and } \quad y=2 \end{array} $$
